title: Cargo leaves in a bubble
hook: Predict where the cargo ends up, then run the model.

knows: Cells have a plasma membrane separating inside from outside.
doesNotKnow: In exocytosis a vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane, releasing its soluble contents outside the cell. The orange dot is cargo and the ring in the starting picture is its vesicle; this is a simplified model.

misconception: Everything crosses a cell membrane by the same mechanism.
objective: In exocytosis a vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane, releasing its soluble contents outside the cell. The orange dot is cargo and the ring in the starting picture is its vesicle; this is a simplified model.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: A vesicle inside a cell fuses with its plasma membrane during exocytosis. Where is its soluble cargo released? In exocytosis a vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane, releasing its soluble contents outside the cell. The orange dot is cargo and the ring in the starting picture is its vesicle; this is a simplified model.
Recall: What happens to the soluble contents of a vesicle during exocytosis? Fusion with the plasma membrane releases soluble vesicle contents outside.
The diagram is schematic and represents only selected molecules, not trajectories or all particles.

recall.question: What happens to the soluble contents of a vesicle during exocytosis?
recall.why: Fusion with the plasma membrane releases soluble vesicle contents outside.
